## Paper Information

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Title | WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution |
| Authors | Hang He, Linting Wang, Guanming Liu, Bo Mao, Jinxiu Liu, Yiran Suo, Maosen Zhou, Zhiheng Xi, Guanting Dong, Zhou Shao, Rui Zheng, Jie Zhou, Chengcheng Wan, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang |
| Venue | arXiv |
| Year | 2026 |
| Topic | Long-horizon cowork agents, recursive environment evolution, verifier-to-turn credit assignment |
| Paper Link | [arXiv:2610.18067v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18067v1) |
| Project | [WorkRover](https://workrover.github.io/) |
| Original Asset License | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), as linked from the arXiv record. |
| Asset Type | 4 method figures, 4 result figures, 0 tables |
| Method Figures PPT | [Download all 4 editable figures](method_figures/method_figures_editable.pptx) |

Figures are attributed to the authors above. Previews are cropped reproductions of the paper figures; editable reconstructions and plotting code are adaptations created for ReFigure, under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

PPTX reconstructions preserve native text and vector geometry; mathematical glyphs in Figures 2, 3 and 5 use editable outlines. Icons, logos and five small hatch fills remain independent raster objects. Arrows are editable freeform paths whose endpoints are not bound to modules. Calibri is retained; Aptos labels use Arial. Native shadows, gradients and dash spacing are approximate. Final PPTX files were rendered and visually checked with Artifact Tool; PowerPoint application compatibility was not tested.

### Plotting Code

All 35 values are transcribed from the printed annotations; no measured value is estimated. Bar geometry, five-panel arrangement, model logos, shared legend and palette follow the approved figure. The original small logos are embedded raster crops; typography and subtle shadows are a reconstruction.

```python
import base64
import io

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle, PathPatch
from matplotlib.path import Path
import matplotlib.image as mpimg

# Paper: WorkRover, arXiv:2610.18067v1, Figure 1.
# All numerical data below are transcribed from printed figure annotations.
# Calibri matches the paper; installed sans-serif fallbacks remain portable.
plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": ["Calibri", "Arial", "DejaVu Sans"],
                     "savefig.facecolor": "white", "svg.fonttype": "none"})
DPI = 200
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 2957, 1257
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(WIDTH / DPI, HEIGHT / DPI), dpi=DPI,
                 facecolor="white")
ax = fig.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1])
ax.set(xlim=(0, WIDTH), ylim=(HEIGHT, 0))
ax.set_axis_off()

# Original small logos/icons are embedded PNGs, not generated substitutes.
# The charts, all labels, and numeric annotations remain Matplotlib objects.
ICON_PNG = {
    "WorkRover": "",
    "Qwen": "",
    "GPT": "",
    "GLM": "",
    "Claude": "",
    "Kimi": ""
}

def icon(name, x, y, width, height=None):
    image = mpimg.imread(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(ICON_PNG[name])))
    height = width if height is None else height
    ax.imshow(image, extent=(x, x + width, y + height, y),
              interpolation="lanczos", aspect="auto", zorder=4)

def label(text, x, y, pixels, color="black", bold=False, ha="center"):
    return ax.text(x, y, text, fontsize=pixels * 72 / DPI,
                   fontstyle="italic", fontweight="bold" if bold else "normal",
                   color=color, ha=ha, va="baseline", linespacing=0.90,
                   zorder=5)

# Model orders follow the original figure; the last four vary by benchmark.
panels = [
    ("JobBench", [36.89, 10.62, 21.80, 38.30, 43.40, 44.50, 54.27],
     ["WorkRover", "Qwen3.5", "Qwen3.6", "GPT", "GLM", "Claude", "Kimi"],
     [253, 359, 465, 607, 713, 819, 925], 466, 353, 547, False),
    ("GDPval", [1218, 805, 1069, 1396, 1396, 1418, 1572],
     ["WorkRover", "Qwen3.5", "Qwen3.6", "Claude", "GPT", "GLM", "Kimi"],
     [1098, 1204, 1310, 1452, 1558, 1664, 1770], 466, 353, 547, True),
    ("AutomationBench", [28.67, 6.00, 9.67, 9.90, 22.70, 26.17, 46.67],
     ["WorkRover", "Qwen3.5", "Qwen3.6", "Claude", "GPT", "GLM", "Kimi"],
     [1944, 2050, 2156, 2297, 2403, 2510, 2616], 466, 353, 547, False),
    ("WorkBuddy Bench (Office)", [74.13, 60.50, 65.65, 72.18, 79.57, 86.05, 92.51],
     ["WorkRover", "Qwen3.5", "Qwen3.6", "Kimi", "GLM", "GPT", "Claude"],
     [676, 782, 888, 1029, 1135, 1242, 1348], 1057, 353, 1138, False),
    ("OfficeQA Pro", [48.87, 19.55, 44.36, 41.40, 46.60, 57.10, 63.30],
     ["WorkRover", "Qwen3.5", "Qwen3.6", "GLM", "Claude", "GPT", "Kimi"],
     [1521, 1627, 1733, 1875, 1981, 2087, 2193], 1057, 342, 1138, False),
]
COLORS = ["#4169ff", "#00b6e8", "#f0f0f0"]
BAR_WIDTH = 83

def top_rounded_bar(x, y, width, bottom, color, alpha=1, radius=16, zorder=2):
    # Only the top corners are rounded; baseline corners stay square.
    r = min(radius, (bottom - y) / 2)
    vertices = [(x, bottom), (x, y+r), (x, y), (x+r, y),
                (x+width-r, y), (x+width, y), (x+width, y+r),
                (x+width, bottom), (x, bottom)]
    codes = [Path.MOVETO, Path.LINETO, Path.CURVE3, Path.CURVE3,
             Path.LINETO, Path.CURVE3, Path.CURVE3, Path.LINETO, Path.CLOSEPOLY]
    ax.add_patch(PathPatch(Path(vertices, codes), facecolor=color, edgecolor="none",
                           alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder))

for title, values, models, xs, baseline, tallest, title_y, integer in panels:
    for i, (value, model, x) in enumerate(zip(values, models, xs)):
        top = baseline - tallest * value / max(values)
        if i == 0:
            # A small layered shadow mirrors the highlighted method bars.
            for spread, opacity in [(9, 0.025), (6, 0.05), (3, 0.10)]:
                top_rounded_bar(x+6-spread/2, top+6-spread/2,
                                BAR_WIDTH+spread, baseline+6+spread/2,
                                "#203055", opacity, zorder=1)
        top_rounded_bar(x, top, BAR_WIDTH, baseline, COLORS[min(i, 2)])
        text = f"{int(value)}" if integer else f"{value:.2f}"
        if i < 2:
            label(text, x+BAR_WIDTH/2, top-20, 45.98, bold=True)
        else:
            label(text, x+BAR_WIDTH/2, top+50, 38.91, color="#666666")
        name = "Qwen" if model.startswith("Qwen") else model
        if name == "WorkRover":
            icon(name, x+8, top-132, 67, 56)
        else:
            icon(name, x+9.5, top-(152 if i == 1 else 90), 64)
    left, right = xs[0]-12, xs[-1]+BAR_WIDTH+12
    ax.plot([left, right], [baseline, baseline], color="#333333", lw=1.5, zorder=6)
    divider = (xs[2]+BAR_WIDTH+xs[3])/2
    ax.plot([divider, divider], [baseline-452, baseline],
            color="#aab4c3", lw=1.0, dashes=(3.2, 3.2), zorder=1)
    label(title, (left+right)/2, title_y, 63.67, color="#333333", bold=True)

# A single complete shared legend, in the paper's model order.
legend = [
    ("WorkRover", "WorkRover-35B-A3B", 143.40, COLORS[0], True),
    ("Qwen", "Qwen3.5-35B-A3B", 711.00, COLORS[1], False),
    ("Qwen", "Qwen3.6-27B", 1224.19, COLORS[2], False),
    ("GPT", "GPT-5.5", 1641.02, COLORS[2], False),
    ("Claude", "Claude Opus 4.7", 1947.34, COLORS[2], False),
    ("GLM", "GLM-5.2", 2419.95, COLORS[2], False),
    ("Kimi", "Kimi K3", 2739.05, COLORS[2], False),
]
for name, text, x, color, bold in legend:
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x-88, 1204), 20, 20, facecolor=color,
                           edgecolor="#333333", lw=0.7))
    if name == "WorkRover":
        icon(name, x-54, 1198, 44, 37)
    else:
        icon(name, x-55, 1196, 42)
    label(text, x, 1234, 49.78, bold=bold, ha="left")

# Axes are intentionally hidden as in the original; each panel has its own scale.
fig.savefig("fig1_reconstructed.png", dpi=DPI)
fig.savefig("fig1_reconstructed.svg")
plt.close(fig)
```

All 21 category shares and three skill totals are transcribed from the approved figure. The treemap arrangement and palette are reproduced with editable rectangles and text; original category icons are embedded as small raster images. Published percentages are rounded and are not renormalized. Typography and spacing are approximate; illustrations remain raster objects.

```python
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")

from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle, PathPatch

# Paper: WorkRover, arXiv:2610.18067v1, Figure 4.

                     "savefig.facecolor": "white", "svg.fonttype": "none"})
DPI = 200
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 1994, 639
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(WIDTH / DPI, HEIGHT / DPI), dpi=DPI,

    "finance": "",

def icon(name, x, y, width, height=None):
    image = mpimg.imread(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(ICON_PNG[name])))
    height = width if height is None else height
    ax.imshow(image, extent=(x, x + width, y + height, y),
              interpolation="lanczos", aspect="auto", zorder=4)

def label(text, x, y, pixels, color="black", bold=False, ha="center"):
    return ax.text(x, y, text, fontsize=pixels * 72 / DPI,
                   fontstyle="italic", fontweight="bold" if bold else "normal",

# Shares are printed to 0.1%; File/App totals may sum to 100.1% from rounding.
# Preserve the published percentages rather than silently renormalizing them.

              "Development & cloud": 21.4, "Content, design & media": 7.9,
              "Finance & markets": 7.0, "Social & communication": 7.4,
              "Marketing, sales & CRM": 5.8}
colors = {"purple": "#452c7a", "blue": "#3a518a", "teal": "#208e8b",

          "other": "#e4e8ee"}

         "other": "#b5beca"}
```

### Plotting Code

All 25 bar values and the five gain annotations below are transcribed from Figure 6 (PDF page 9), at the precision printed in the paper. This is reconstructed plotting code, not the authors' original implementation. GDPval v2 uses Elo; the other panels use percentages.

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

# Values are exact transcriptions of the printed Figure 6 labels.
methods = ["Backbone", "SFT", "Backbone + E-GRPO",
           "SFT + E-GRPO", "SFT + VTCA"]
panels = [
    ("JobBench", [10.6, 25.0, 19.0, 33.5, 36.9], 40,
     [0, 10, 20, 30, 40], "Score (%)", "Δ +3.4"),
    ("GDPval v2", [805, 1060, 960, 1175, 1218], 1650,
     [0, 400, 800, 1200, 1600], "Elo", "Δ +43 Elo"),
    ("AutomationBench", [6.0, 15.5, 11.5, 23.0, 28.7], 35,
     [0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35], "Score (%)", "Δ +5.7"),
    ("WorkBuddy (Office)", [60.5, 68.0, 65.0, 71.5, 74.1], 80,
     [0, 20, 40, 60, 80], "Score (%)", "Δ +2.6"),
    ("OfficeQA Pro", [19.6, 34.0, 28.0, 43.5, 48.9], 60,
     [0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60], "Score (%)", "Δ +5.4"),
]
colors = ["#eaf3e2", "#b4deb6", "#7bc6be", "#439cc4", "#0868a6"]
available = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
family = "Calibri" if "Calibri" in available else "DejaVu Sans"
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": family, "font.style": "italic", "font.size": 18,
    "axes.labelsize": 20, "xtick.labelsize": 18, "ytick.labelsize": 18,
    "savefig.facecolor": "white", "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "pdf.fonttype": 42, "ps.fonttype": 42,
})

# Explicit panel bounds preserve the source's wide five-panel composition.
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18.0, 18.0 * 115 / 466), dpi=180)
lefts = [92.028, 185.770, 279.512, 373.254, 466.996]
for idx, (title, values, upper, ticks, label, gain) in enumerate(panels):
    ax = fig.add_axes([(lefts[idx] - 74) / 466, (291 - 282.278) / 115,
                       69.439 / 466, 71.754 / 115])
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e1e6ec", linewidth=0.65)
    ax.bar(np.arange(5), values, width=1.0, color=colors,
           edgecolor="#2d414d", linewidth=2.1, zorder=3)
    ax.set_xlim(-1.6667, 5.6667)
    ax.set_ylim(0, upper)
    ax.set_yticks(ticks)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_xlabel(label, labelpad=1)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=3.1, width=1.5, pad=3, colors="black")
    for spine in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    for spine in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_color("#8b97a3")
        ax.spines[spine].set_linewidth(1.65)
    for x, value in enumerate(values):
        text = f"{int(value)}" if label == "Elo" else f"{value:.1f}"
        # Four-digit Elo labels use a slightly smaller size to keep the
        # adjacent 1175 and 1218 annotations separate at gallery width.
        number_size = 13.0 if label == "Elo" else 14.7
        text_x = x + ({3: -0.08, 4: 0.08}.get(x, 0) if label == "Elo" else 0)
        ax.text(text_x, value + upper * 0.018, text, ha="center", va="bottom",
                fontsize=number_size, fontstyle="italic", clip_on=False)
    ax.text(0.5, 1.016, gain, transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=18, clip_on=False)
    fig.text((lefts[idx] + 69.439 / 2 - 74) / 466, 0.839,
             title, ha="center", va="center", color="#1c2943",
             fontsize=20.5, fontweight="bold", fontstyle="italic")

fig.legend([Patch(facecolor=color, edgecolor="none") for color in colors],
```

### Plotting Code

Note: The following code is an approximate visual reconstruction based on the provided figure. The displayed values in panels (a), (b), and (c) are transcribed exactly from Figure 7 (PDF page 10). Panel (b)'s unlabelled error-bar endpoints and panel (d)'s unlabelled step-curve values are digitized from the PDF's vector paths against the plotted axes; they reproduce the published geometry and are approximate, not experimental raw data. The paper does not identify the statistical interpretation of panel (b)'s error bars, so the code retains their visible endpoints without assigning a confidence level. C = Context, T = Task, H = Harness, V = Verifier.

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

available = {font.name for font in font_manager.fontManager.ttflist}
family = "Calibri" if "Calibri" in available else "DejaVu Sans"
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": family, "font.style": "italic", "font.size": 17,
    "axes.labelsize": 19, "xtick.labelsize": 18, "ytick.labelsize": 18,
    "figure.facecolor": "white", "savefig.facecolor": "white",
    "pdf.fonttype": 42, "ps.fonttype": 42,
})
ink, spine, grid = "#17233e", "#566477", "#eef1f5"
blue, green = "#619fd2", "#58b668"
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18.0, 18.0 * 141 / 470), dpi=180)
# Panel bounds follow the original PDF geometry; no automatic layout changes.
rectangles = [(95.686, 184.514), (208.027, 302.081),
              (329.513, 419.648), (443.161, 537.215)]
axes = [fig.add_axes([(left - 71) / 470, (219 - 197.480) / 141,
                      (right - left) / 470, 84.910 / 141])
        for left, right in rectangles]

def style_axis(ax, ylim, yticks, ylabel):
    ax.set_ylim(*ylim)
    ax.set_yticks(yticks)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, labelpad=5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=grid, linewidth=2.3)
    for name in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[name].set_visible(False)
    for name in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[name].set_color(spine)
        ax.spines[name].set_linewidth(3.1)
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", length=4.5, width=3.0, color=spine, pad=4)

titles = ["(a) Joint revision necessity", "(b) Safe repair outcomes",
          "(c) Repair reliability\nacross generations",
          "(d) Task success\nacross repair iterations"]
for (left, _), title in zip(rectangles, titles):
    fig.text((left - 71) / 470 - 0.043, 0.982, title,
             ha="left", va="top", fontsize=21, fontweight="bold",
             fontstyle="italic", linespacing=1.18)

# (a): exact values printed above the six bars.
ax = axes[0]
joint = np.array([0.64, 0.71, 0.48, 0.67, 0.55, 0.74])
joint_colors = ["#e2edc9", "#a4d3b7", "#65c4b9",
                "#26a7c8", "#607bbc", "#345e84"]
x = np.arange(6)
ax.bar(x, joint, width=0.68, color=joint_colors,
       edgecolor=ink, linewidth=1.25)
style_axis(ax, (0, 1.04), [0, 0.5, 1], "Joint necessity")
ax.set_xlim(-0.55, 5.55)
ax.set_xticks(x, ["CT", "CH", "CV", "TH", "TV", "HV"])
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f"{y:g}"))
for position, value in zip(x, joint):
    ax.text(position, value + 0.025, f"{value:.2f}",
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=18)
ax.text(0.5, 1.065, "Frozen proposals", transform=ax.transAxes,
        ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=16)

# (b): exact annotated safe-resolution percentages.
ax = axes[1]
safe = np.array([3.0, 39.3, 55.0, 60.7, 70.3]) / 100
x = np.arange(5)
ax.bar(x, safe, width=0.74, color=green, edgecolor=ink, linewidth=1.25)
ax.bar(x, 1 - safe, bottom=safe, width=0.74, color="#cce9ac",
       edgecolor=ink, linewidth=1.25)
# Approximate digitization of the PDF's unlabelled errorbar endpoints.
# These are visible bounds, not a claim about statistical confidence level.
lower = np.array([0.014, 0.339, 0.494, 0.551, 0.650])
upper = np.array([0.055, 0.449, 0.605, 0.660, 0.753])
ax.errorbar(x, safe, yerr=np.vstack([safe - lower, upper - safe]),
            fmt="none", ecolor=ink, elinewidth=2.0,
            capsize=4.3, capthick=2.0, zorder=4)
style_axis(ax, (0, 1.04), [0, 0.5, 1], "Fraction of triggers")
ax.set_xlim(-0.55, 4.55)
ax.set_xticks(x, ["Parent", "Local", "Seq", "Regen", "FCR"])
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f"{y:g}"))
for position, value in zip(x, safe):
    y = 0.070 if value < 0.1 else value * 0.5
    ax.text(position, y, f"{value * 100:.1f}", ha="center",
            va="bottom" if value < 0.1 else "center",
            fontsize=18, fontweight="bold")
ax.legend([Patch(facecolor=green, edgecolor=ink, linewidth=1.2),
           Patch(facecolor="#cce9ac", edgecolor=ink, linewidth=1.2)],
          ["Safe resolution", "Not safely resolved"],
          loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(-0.015, 1.045),
          ncol=2, fontsize=14.3, frameon=False, handlelength=0.85,
          handletextpad=0.30, columnspacing=0.45, borderaxespad=0)

# (c): exact annotated percentages; filled-outlined markers match the figure.
ax = axes[2]
generations = np.arange(1, 4)
srr = np.array([70.3, 72.4, 71.8])
audit = np.array([93.8, 94.6, 94.2])
ax.plot(generations, srr, color=blue, linewidth=3.1,
        marker="o", markersize=7.7, markerfacecolor="white",
        markeredgecolor=blue, markeredgewidth=3.1)
ax.plot(generations, audit, color=green, linewidth=3.1, linestyle="--",
        marker="s", markersize=7.7, markerfacecolor="white",
        markeredgecolor=green, markeredgewidth=3.1)
style_axis(ax, (60, 102), [60, 80, 100], "Rate (%)")
ax.set_xlim(0.65, 3.35)
ax.set_xticks(generations)
ax.set_xlabel("Construction generation", labelpad=7)
for values in (srr, audit):
    for generation, value in zip(generations, values):
        ax.text(generation, value + 1.6, f"{value:.1f}",
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=18)
handles = [Line2D([], [], color=blue, marker="o", markersize=7,
                  markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=3, linewidth=3),
           Line2D([], [], color=green, marker="s", markersize=7,
                  markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=3,
                  linewidth=3, linestyle="--")]
ax.legend(handles, ["SRR", "Audit Pass"], loc="lower center",
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.045), ncol=2, fontsize=16,
          frameon=False, handlelength=1.0, handletextpad=0.25,
          columnspacing=0.4, borderaxespad=0)

# (d): approximate digitization from the PDF's plotted vector paths.
# Original raw measurements are unavailable. Values are not new experiments.
iterations = np.arange(6)
curves = [
    ("FCR", [35, 47, 54, 59, 63, 65], blue, "o", "-"),
    ("Greedy", [35, 42, 47, 50, 52, 53], "#65d1d2", "s", "--"),
    ("Local", [35, 39, 41, 42, 43, 43], "#f07f0f", "^", ":"),
    ("Regen", [35, 43, 48, 52, 55, 57], "#f76666", "D", "-."),
]
ax = axes[3]
for label, values, color, marker, linestyle in curves:
    ax.plot(iterations, values, drawstyle="steps-post", label=label,
            color=color, linewidth=3.1, linestyle=linestyle,
            marker=marker, markersize=8.2,
            markerfacecolor=color, markeredgecolor=color,
            markeredgewidth=1.7)
style_axis(ax, (20, 80), [20, 40, 60, 80], "Rollout success (%)")
ax.set_xlim(-0.1, 5.12)
ax.set_xticks(iterations)
ax.set_xlabel("Repair iteration", labelpad=7)
ax.legend(loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.045),
          ncol=4, fontsize=15.4, frameon=False, handlelength=1.0,
          handletextpad=0.15, columnspacing=0.5, borderaxespad=0)

fig.savefig("workrover_fig7_reconstructed.png", dpi=240)
plt.show()
```
